summary: July's shock payroll loss of 23,000 jobs has cooled rate-hike bets going into this week, with Wednesday's CPI report now the week's clearest test of the roughly 56% market-implied odds the Fed pauses at its September meeting. A new 12.5% Section 301 tariff on Chinese goods took effect July 24, raising the overall tariff burden on China by 2.5%, keeping the dollar under pressure and supporting gold's outperformance.
tweet: Weak jobs killed the September hike; now Wednesday's CPI decides if that reprieve holds — gold and stocks both pricing in a soft landing, tariff drag and all.
